pulls.author: erifan

pulls.author: hgqxjj
pulls.body_excerpt: **Description:** StoreNode::Ideal() only removes an earlier store when a later store of the same or larger size writes to the same address. pulls.author: merykitty
pulls.body_excerpt: Hi, In principle, to hoist a store out of a loop, you need to peel the loop first, then move the store up past the entry of the first iteration. As a result, removing a store after peeling is a strictly more general transformation. Assume `p` and `p1` are independent, `p` and `v` are loop-invariants, we have: 0. loop (0..n) { Store(p1, v1); Store(p, v); StoreLoadFence(); } 1. Peel the first iteration Store(p1, v1); Store(p, v); StoreLoadFence(); loop (1..n) { Store(p1, v1); Store(p, v); StoreLoadFence(); } 2.
